topics.title: Reading +, −, and = symbols

topics.description: Add three one-digit numbers using strategies including looking for pairs that make 10

topics.description: Add and subtract two two-digit numbers using concrete objects, pictorial representations, and mental methods

topics.title: Addition and subtraction strategies
topics.description: Use counting on and counting back as strategies for addition and subtraction

topics.title: Addition and subtraction within 20
topics.description: Add and subtract within 20 using strategies such as making ten, decomposing a number leading to ten, and using known facts

topics.description: Understand and apply the commutative property of addition: addends can be added in any order

topics.title: Fluent adding and subtracting within 10

topics.description: Recall and use addition and subtraction facts to 20 fluently, and derive and use related facts up to 100

topics.description: Understand and apply the associative property of addition: when adding three numbers, any two can be added first

topics.title: Inverse: addition undoes subtraction
topics.description: Recognise and use the inverse relationship between addition and subtraction to check calculations and solve missing-number problems

topics.title: Mental addition and subtraction
topics.description: Add and subtract a two-digit number and ones mentally and using concrete/pictorial representations

topics.title: Mental and written addition and subtraction
topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction problems using mental and written methods, including problems involving numbers, quantities, and measures

topics.title: Subtracting multiples of 10
topics.description: Subtract multiples of 10 (10–90) from multiples of 10 using place value strategies

topics.title: Three-number word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems that call for adding three whole numbers with a total of 20 or less, representing the problem with objects, a drawing or a three-part bar model and with an equation that uses a symbol for the unknown total (e.g. 4 + 7 + 6 = ☐); choose a convenient order or grouping to add (such as making 10 first) and give the answer in the context of the problem

topics.title: Unknown in Addition & Subtraction
topics.description: Determine the unknown whole number in an addition or subtraction equation relating three whole numbers

topics.title: What the equals sign means
topics.description: Understand the meaning of the equal sign as 'is the same as' and determine if equations are true or false

topics.title: Adding and subtracting
topics.description: Add and subtract numbers with up to three digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction

topics.title: Adding numbers
topics.description: Add up to four two-digit numbers using strategies based on place value and properties of operations

topics.title: Addition and subtraction strategies
topics.description: Explain why addition and subtraction strategies work, using place value and the properties of operations

topics.title: Addition and subtraction within 1000
topics.description: Add and subtract within 1000 using concrete models, drawings, and strategies based on place value; understand composing and decomposing tens and hundreds

topics.title: Fluent adding and subtracting within 100
topics.description: Fluently add and subtract within 100 using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction

topics.title: Fluent adding and subtracting within 20
topics.description: Fluently add and subtract within 20 using mental strategies; know from memory all sums of two one-digit numbers

topics.description: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and ones

topics.title: Mentally adding hundreds to 3-digit numbers
topics.description: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and hundreds

topics.title: Mentally adding tens to 3-digit numbers
topics.description: Mentally add and subtract a three-digit number and tens

topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction problems including missing-number problems, using number facts, place value, and more complex methods

topics.title: Numbers on a number line
topics.description: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line and represent sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram

topics.title: Two-Step Word Problems
topics.description: Solve one- and two-step word problems within 100 using addition and subtraction, with unknowns in all positions

topics.title: Adding and subtracting
topics.description: Add and subtract numbers with up to four digits using formal written methods of columnar addition and subtraction

topics.title: Fluent adding and subtracting within 1000
topics.description: Fluently add and subtract within 1000 using strategies and algorithms based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction

topics.title: Two-step addition and subtraction problems
topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction two-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why

topics.title: Two-Step Equations
topics.description: Solve two-step word problems using the four operations; represent problems using equations with a letter standing for the unknown quantity

topics.title: Adding and subtracting
topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why

topics.title: Adding and subtracting decimals
topics.description: Add and subtract decimals to hundredths using strategies based on place value, properties of operations, and the relationship between addition and subtraction; relate strategies to written methods and explain reasoning

topics.title: Checking Answers by Rounding
topics.description: Use rounding to check answers to calculations and determine appropriate levels of accuracy in context

topics.title: Fluent addition and subtraction
topics.description: Fluently add and subtract whole numbers with more than four digits using the standard columnar algorithm

topics.title: Mental addition and subtraction
topics.description: Add and subtract numbers mentally with increasingly large numbers, using place-value knowledge and derived facts

topics.title: Adding and subtracting
topics.description: Solve addition and subtraction multi-step problems in contexts, deciding which operations and methods to use and why, with numbers up to 10,000,000 and decimals

topics.title: Positive and Negative Numbers
topics.description: Understand positive and negative numbers as describing quantities with opposite directions or values; use them in context such as temperature, floors in a building, and bank balances

topics.title: Changing and fixed amounts
topics.description: Identify quantities that can change and quantities that stay the same within a stated real-life situation and time period, and explain why: on one school bus trip the number of seats stays the same while the number of passengers changes from stop to stop. 'Stays the same' describes that situation and time, not something that can never change

topics.title: Describing growing number patterns
topics.description: Recognise, describe and create additive patterns that increase or decrease by a constant amount using numbers, shapes and objects, state the rule, and find missing elements

topics.title: Finding the repeating unit
topics.description: Identify and describe the repeating unit (core) of a repeating pattern made with numbers, symbols, shapes or objects, and use it to continue, create, compare and translate patterns from one form (movements, sounds) into another (objects, shapes, letters or numbers)

topics.title: What a symbol stands for
topics.description: Recognise when a symbol (a box, shape, question mark or letter) is being used to stand for a number, and describe how it is being used: as an unknown number to be found, or as a quantity that can change

topics.title: Following number algorithms
topics.description: Follow and create algorithms (flowcharts or written step lists) with a sequence of steps, decisions using comparisons (e.g. 'Is the number greater than 20?', 'Is it even?') and repetition until a stop condition, to investigate numbers and describe the patterns that emerge

topics.title: Numbers on a number line
topics.description: Understand inequalities as statements comparing expressions, represent solutions on a number line, and solve simple linear inequalities using the same inverse-operation methods as equations

topics.title: Designing number algorithms
topics.description: Design and use algorithms with a sequence of steps, decisions with several alternatives (if / else-if / else) and repetition that apply rules to generate sets of numbers, implementing them in a flowchart, spreadsheet or visual program, and explain the patterns produced

topics.title: Equations with Two Unknowns
topics.description: Find pairs of numbers that satisfy an equation with two unknowns (e.g. find pairs (a, b) where a + b = 10 or 2a + b = 15)

topics.title: Linear number sequences
topics.description: Generate and describe constant-step (linear) number sequences whose terms include negative values (counting through and past zero) or whose step is a decimal, using signed-number and decimal addition and subtraction; state the term-to-term rule, continue the sequence and use the rule to find a later term

topics.title: Number Pattern Relationships
topics.description: Generate two numerical patterns using two given rules; identify relationships between corresponding terms; form ordered pairs and graph them on a coordinate plane

topics.title: Systematic Listing
topics.description: Enumerate possibilities of combinations of two variables systematically (e.g. all ways to choose from a set of options)

topics.title: Using Simple Formulae
topics.description: Use simple formulae expressed in words or symbols to calculate values (e.g. perimeter = 2 × (length + width))

topics.title: Writing Algebraic Equations
topics.description: Express missing number problems algebraically using letters for unknowns; translate word problems into equations

topics.title: Algebraic Notation
topics.description: Use and interpret algebraic notation including: ab for a × b, 3y for y + y + y, a² for a × a, a/b for a ÷ b, coefficients as fractions, and brackets for grouping; read and write algebraic expressions fluently

topics.title: Algebraic Transformations
topics.description: Model situations or procedures by translating them into algebraic expressions or formulae and by using graphs; move between word problems, algebraic representations, tables, and graphical representations

topics.title: Collecting Like Terms
topics.description: Simplify algebraic expressions by collecting like terms — combine terms with the same variable and power (e.g., 3a + 2b + 5a = 8a + 2b) while maintaining equivalence

topics.title: Coordinates
topics.description: Plot and read coordinates in all four quadrants of the Cartesian plane, using positive and negative x- and y-values to describe positions precisely

topics.title: Expanding Single Brackets
topics.description: Expand (multiply out) a single term over a bracket using the distributive property, e.g., 3(2x + 5) = 6x + 15; expand expressions involving negative multipliers

topics.title: Expressions & Equations Vocabulary
topics.description: Understand and use the concepts and vocabulary of expressions, equations, inequalities, terms, and factors; distinguish between an expression (no equals sign), an equation (equals sign), and an inequality (inequality sign)

topics.title: Generating Sequences
topics.description: Generate terms of a sequence from a term-to-term rule (e.g., 'add 3 each time') or a position-to-term rule (e.g., '2n + 1'), and identify whether a sequence is arithmetic, geometric, or neither

topics.title: Solving Linear Equations
topics.description: Use algebraic methods to solve linear equations in one variable, including equations that require rearrangement, expanding brackets, and collecting terms on both sides; solve equations with rational number coefficients

topics.title: Substituting into Formulae
topics.description: Substitute numerical values into formulae and expressions including scientific formulae; evaluate expressions by replacing variables with given values and computing the result using correct order of operations

topics.title: Factorising Expressions
topics.description: Factorise algebraic expressions by taking out common factors — identify the highest common factor of all terms and write the expression as a product, e.g., 6x + 9 = 3(2x + 3)

topics.title: Linear Function Graphs
topics.description: Recognise that a linear function produces a straight-line graph, understand the relationship between an equation of the form y = mx + c and its graphical representation, and interpret gradient and y-intercept in context

topics.title: Nth-Term Rules
topics.description: Find the nth-term expression for an arithmetic sequence by identifying the common difference and the zero-term, and use it to determine any term in the sequence or test whether a given number belongs to the sequence

topics.title: Plotting Linear Graphs
topics.description: Plot linear graphs by generating a table of values, reduce a two-variable linear equation to the form y = mx + c, and calculate gradients from two points on a line

topics.title: Simple formulae
topics.description: Understand and use standard mathematical formulae; rearrange formulae to change the subject, performing inverse operations to isolate a different variable

topics.title: Estimating answers
topics.description: Use graphs of linear and quadratic functions to estimate output values for given inputs, find approximate solutions to equations, and interpret graphical information in real-world contexts

topics.title: Expanding Double Brackets
topics.description: Expand products of two or more binomials, e.g., (x + 3)(x - 2) = x² + x - 6, using the grid method or FOIL; simplify the result by collecting like terms

topics.title: Quadratic Graphs
topics.description: Recognise that quadratic functions produce curved (parabolic) graphs, distinguish them from linear graphs, and use plotted quadratic graphs to estimate values and find approximate solutions

topics.title: Simultaneous Equations
topics.description: Understand that two linear equations can be solved simultaneously by finding the point where their graphs intersect, and interpret this graphically and algebraically as the pair of values satisfying both equations

topics.title: Comparing groups: more or fewer
topics.description: Compare two groups of objects to determine which has more, fewer, or whether they are equal, using matching and counting strategies

topics.title: How Many in Total?
topics.description: Cardinality principle: the last number said when counting a set tells how many objects are in the set, regardless of arrangement or order counted

topics.title: One More Each Time
topics.description: Each successive counting number represents a quantity that is one larger than the previous number

topics.title: One-to-one counting
topics.description: One-to-one correspondence when counting objects: each object is paired with exactly one number name

topics.title: Representing numbers with objects
topics.description: Represent numbers using objects, pictorial representations, and the number line

topics.title: Two written numerals between 1 and 10
topics.description: Compare two written numerals between 1 and 10 to determine which is greater or less

topics.title: Counting in 2s
topics.description: Count in multiples of 2, 5, and 10 (skip counting)

topics.title: Counting objects to 20
topics.description: Count a set of objects to answer 'how many?' for sets up to 20 (arranged in lines, arrays, circles, or scattered)

topics.title: Rote counting to 100
topics.description: Rote count forwards and backwards from 0 to 100, beginning from 0, 1, or any given number, by ones

topics.title: Seeing parts within 10
topics.description: Use subitising to recognise and name the parts of a collection up to 10 and combine them — e.g. seeing 7 on a ten frame as 5 and 2, or a domino as 3 and 3 — connecting part-part-whole thinking to quick recognition

topics.title: Subitising to 5
topics.description: Recognise and name the number of objects in a collection of up to 5 instantly, without counting one by one (subitising), using dot patterns, dice faces, fingers and small groups of objects

topics.title: Counting big collections in groups
topics.description: Quantify collections of up to 120 objects by partitioning them into equal groups (twos, fives or tens) and skip counting, explaining why grouping makes counting faster and more reliable

topics.title: Counting forwards and backwards
topics.description: Count forwards and backwards in steps of 3 from 0

topics.title: Counting forwards and backwards
topics.description: Count forwards and backwards in tens from any number (not just multiples of 10)

topics.title: Counting Within 1,000
topics.description: Count within 1000, including skip-counting by 5s, 10s, and 100s

topics.title: Skip Counting (4s, 8s, 50s, 100s)
topics.description: Count from 0 in multiples of 4, 8, 50, and 100

topics.title: Counting in 6s
topics.description: Count in multiples of 6, 7, 9, 25, and 1000

topics.title: Pictograms and tally charts
topics.description: Interpret and construct simple pictograms, tally charts, block diagrams, and simple tables, including giving displays a title, labels and the source of the data

topics.title: Sorting into categories
topics.description: Classify objects into given categories, count the number in each category, and sort the categories by count

topics.title: Carrying out a statistical investigation
topics.description: Carry out a statistical investigation for a given question of interest: collect categorical or discrete numerical data (for example by observation or survey), record and represent it in a suitable display (by hand or with digital tools) and interpret the results in terms of the question

topics.title: Collecting data for a question
topics.description: Acquire categorical and discrete numerical data to address a question of interest by observing, collecting or accessing a data set, and record it using appropriate methods including frequency tables and spreadsheets

topics.title: Comparing results from two groups
topics.description: Predict whether the category counts from one group (e.g. a class tally of favourite fruit) will be the same in a different group of the same size, collect or check the second group's counts, compare the two tallies or pictographs category by category, and explain why equal-size groups can still give different counts

topics.title: Pictograms and tally charts
topics.description: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of data collection and display — data, tally, tally chart, frequency, frequency table, survey, pictogram, bar chart, axis/axes, scale, label, category, discrete data, continuous data, line graph, pie chart — and apply these terms when collecting, organising, and presenting data

topics.title: Picture & Bar Graphs
topics.description: Draw a picture graph and a bar graph (with single-unit scale) to represent a data set with up to four categories; solve put-together, take-apart, and compare problems using information presented in a bar graph

topics.title: Sorting Data into Categories
topics.description: Organise and represent data with up to three categories by counting objects in each category and sorting categories by quantity

topics.title: Sorting into categories
topics.description: Interpret categorical data by asking and answering questions about totals, how many in each category, and how many more or less one category has than another

topics.title: Choosing displays for a purpose
topics.description: Compare different displays of the same data set (for example a tally chart and a picture graph, or a table and a bar graph), describe what is common and what each display makes easy to see, and choose the display that best suits a question or purpose

topics.title: Finding the mode
topics.description: Identify the mode of a data set shown in a tally, pictograph, concrete graph, bar graph, line plot or table: every value or category that occurs most often, so a data set can have one mode or several tied modes; use the convention that there is no mode when every value occurs exactly once; explain what the mode tells about the data; and compare the modes of two data sets

topics.title: Sorting data by two attributes
topics.description: Sort and organise data about people or things according to two attributes at the same time using a Venn diagram (with an overlap), a Carroll diagram or two-way table, or a two-way tally table, and read and answer questions from these logic diagrams and tables

topics.title: Bar graphs
topics.description: Interpret and present discrete and continuous data using appropriate graphical methods, including bar charts and time graphs

topics.title: Calculating the Mean
topics.description: Calculate and interpret the mean as an average of a data set

topics.title: Reading tables
topics.description: Complete, read, and interpret information in tables, including timetables

topics.title: Scaled picture and bar graphs
topics.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set; solve one- and two-step comparison, sum, and difference problems using bar charts, pictograms, and tables

topics.title: Comparing displays and distributions
topics.description: Analyse how effectively different displays or visualisations show and compare data distributions, and describe the shape of a distribution and the variation in the data

topics.title: Finding the median
topics.description: Find the median of a data set by putting the values in order and taking the middle value when there is an odd number of values, or the value halfway between the two middle values when there is an even number (so the median need not be one of the data values and need not be a whole number), and explain that the median is a central value of the ordered data: at least half of the values are at or below it and at least half are at or above it

topics.title: Line graph problems
topics.description: Solve comparison, sum, and difference problems using information presented in a line graph

topics.title: Multiple-bar graphs
topics.description: Construct and read a multiple-bar (grouped) bar graph that shows two or more data sets side by side for the same categories, using a key that maps each colour or pattern to its data set, a title, axis labels and an appropriate scale; compare the data sets within each category and across categories, recognising that bar heights show counts, so when the groups are different sizes a taller bar does not by itself mean a larger share of that group

topics.title: Statistical Analysis Vocabulary
topics.description: Read, write, and use the vocabulary of statistical analysis — mean, median, mode, range, frequency, data, sample, average, chart, table, graph, pie chart, scatter graph, correlation — with understanding of what each term describes

topics.title: Stem-and-leaf plots
topics.description: Organise a data set into a stem-and-leaf plot by splitting each value by place value into a stem (e.g. the tens, or the hundreds and tens for larger values) and a leaf (the next digit), listing the stems in order and every leaf in order on its row, including repeated values, with a key that states the place value (e.g. 4 | 7 = 47); read a stem-and-leaf plot to find values, the least and greatest values, how many values there are, and where values cluster or leave gaps; and compare two data sets shown in separate plots that use the same key

topics.title: Critiquing statistics in the media
topics.description: Identify statistically informed arguments in traditional and digital media and critique their methods, data representations (e.g. truncated axes, distorted pictographs, selective data) and conclusions

topics.title: Line graphs
topics.description: Construct and interpret line graphs for continuous data (e.g. temperature over time, plant growth); read intermediate values, identify trends, and solve comparison and difference problems

topics.title: Line plots with fractions
topics.description: Make a line plot to display a data set of measurements in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); use operations on fractions to solve problems involving data in line plots (e.g. redistribute total equally)

topics.title: Pie charts
topics.description: Interpret and construct pie charts: calculate sector angles from data, draw sectors accurately, and read values from pie charts to solve problems

topics.title: Planning a statistical investigation
topics.description: Plan and conduct a statistical investigation by posing a question or identifying a problem, collecting relevant data, choosing appropriate displays, interpreting the data and communicating findings in context

topics.title: Populations, samples and fair sampling
topics.description: Distinguish a population from a sample drawn from it; explain why a convenient or biased sample (choosing whoever is easiest to reach, volunteers, or a group linked to the answer) can misrepresent the population; explain that random selection gives every member of the population an equal chance of being chosen, which tends to produce representative samples — while recognising that any single random sample can still, by chance, be unrepresentative

topics.title: Stacked-bar graphs
topics.description: Construct and read stacked-bar graphs (vertical or horizontal) in which each bar is divided into segments for the categories of a data set, building each bar by placing every segment on top of the previous one and using a key, title, labels, source and an appropriate scale; read a segment's size as the difference between its top and bottom edges (not the value at its top) and read each bar's total; and compare the make-up of different groups, using bars that show each part as a share of its group's total (a relative-frequency or 100% scale) when the groups are different sizes

topics.title: Validating and describing categorical data
topics.description: Acquire, validate and represent nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete numerical data using software including spreadsheets, process it (totals, differences), and report on the distribution by its mode and shape in context

topics.title: Average distance from the mean
topics.description: Calculate the mean absolute deviation (MAD) of a small numerical data set — find the mean, find each value's distance from the mean (a non-negative number: a value equal to the mean has distance 0), then find the mean of those distances; interpret the MAD as the average distance of the values from the mean, stated in the original units of the data (e.g. minutes, cm, points); and use MADs to compare the spread or consistency of two data sets, recognising that a larger MAD means values typically sit further from the mean and that the MAD is 0 only when every value equals the mean

topics.title: Averages and range
topics.description: Describe, interpret, and compare observed distributions of a single variable using measures of central tendency (mean, median, mode) and spread (range), including choosing a suitable average and the effect of outliers; comparisons describe the observed data sets themselves and do not yet scale the difference in centres by a measure of variability or generalise from samples to wider populations

topics.title: Box plots
topics.description: Construct and interpret a box plot on a numerical scale from a five-number summary (minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile, maximum), using the stated convention that the whiskers extend to the minimum and maximum values; interpret the median, quartiles, IQR and range, recognising that each whisker and each half of the box represents roughly a quarter of the data however long or short it is drawn; explain what a box plot does not show (individual values, clusters, gaps, the number of values, or the mean); and compare two distributions using their box plots

topics.title: Comparing data sets digitally
topics.description: Interpret and compare data sets for nominal and ordinal categorical and discrete and continuous numerical variables using comparative displays (side-by-side column graphs with ordinal categories in a common order, back-to-back dot plots) made with digital tools, processing the data (percentages, ranges) and comparing distributions by mode, range and shape

topics.title: Describing distributions
topics.description: Describe the distribution of a numerical data set by its centre, spread and overall shape — recognising clusters, gaps, peaks, symmetry or skew (a longer tail on one side) and unusual values — and interpret each feature in the context in which the data were collected, recognising that distributions with similar centres can differ greatly in spread and shape

topics.title: Dot plots
topics.description: Construct and interpret dot plots for numerical data sets of any kind (counts, scores, times or measurements), extending earlier measurement line plots: draw a number-line scale with equal intervals that runs from at least the minimum to the maximum value, including values nobody recorded so that gaps stay visible; place one dot per observation, stacking repeated values in evenly spaced columns; label the scale with the attribute and its units; and read the plot to find how often a value occurs, the minimum, maximum and most common values, and the total number of observations, recognising that the height of a stack is a count of observations, not a data value

topics.title: Histograms
topics.description: Construct and interpret histograms for continuous or numerical data grouped into equal-width class intervals on a continuous number-line scale, with no gaps between bars; state the interval-boundary convention used (e.g. 140 ≤ h < 150, so a value of exactly 150 belongs to the next interval); read frequencies from bar heights; describe the distribution shown; and explain how a histogram differs from a bar chart of categories. Unequal-width intervals and frequency density are not included.

topics.title: Pictograms and tally charts
topics.description: Construct and interpret frequency tables, bar charts, pie charts, pictograms, and vertical line charts for both categorical and grouped numerical data, choosing appropriate representations for the data type

topics.title: Quartiles and interquartile range
topics.description: Find the median, lower quartile and upper quartile of a data set using one explicit convention — order the data, find the median, split the data into a lower and an upper half (leaving out the median itself when there is an odd number of values), and take the median of each half as the lower and upper quartile — while recognising that other textbooks, calculators and software may use slightly different conventions; calculate the interquartile range (IQR = upper quartile − lower quartile) and interpret it as the spread of the middle half of the data; and compare what the range and the IQR reveal, including their different sensitivity to extreme values

topics.title: Statistical questions
topics.description: Distinguish a statistical question — one that anticipates variability in the data collected to answer it, so its answer must account for that variability (even when it is reported as a single summary value such as a mean or median) — from a question answered by a single fixed fact; for a statistical question, identify the population (who or what is being asked about), the attribute being investigated, and the variation expected in the answers

topics.title: What was measured, and how
topics.description: Before summarising a numerical data set, state its context precisely: report the number of observations (n) by counting the values in a list or the dots on a dot plot, or by adding the frequencies in a table or histogram (not by counting rows or bars); describe the attribute investigated (what was measured or counted, and for whom or what), how it was measured (the instrument or method and the precision or rounding used, e.g. measured with a tape to the nearest cm versus self-reported) and its units; and use these details to give every summary value with its units and to judge what the data can show, for example recognising when values bunch at round numbers because of how they were recorded

topics.title: Writing a data summary
topics.description: Write a complete summary of a numerical data set in relation to its context, bringing together: the number of observations; the attribute, how it was measured and its units; a measure of centre with a matching measure of variability, each with units, chosen between median with IQR and mean with MAD; the overall pattern and any striking deviations, interpreted in context; and a justification of that choice by the shape of the distribution and the context (e.g. median and IQR for skewed data or data with extreme values, mean and MAD for roughly symmetric data without extreme values)

topics.title: Comparing two populations
topics.description: Use measures of centre and variability calculated from random samples of two populations to make informal comparative inferences about those populations (e.g. whether words in a Grade 7 science book are generally longer than words in a Grade 4 science book): check that each sample was randomly drawn from the population it is meant to describe and is reasonably representative; weigh the difference between the sample centres against the variability within the samples and against how much centres vary from one random sample to another; and state qualified conclusions ('generally', 'on average', 'probably') rather than claiming every member of one population exceeds every member of the other — recognising that a small difference between two samples may be due to chance alone

topics.title: Estimating from a sample
topics.description: Use data from a random sample to estimate a characteristic of the population, such as a proportion, total count, or mean; present the result as an estimate rather than an exact population measurement; state the assumptions the inference relies on (the sample was randomly drawn from the population being described and is reasonably representative) and explain how the conclusion is limited or invalid when those assumptions fail

topics.title: How far apart two groups are
topics.description: Compare two numerical distributions with similar variability shown on a shared scale (e.g. dot plots) in two distinct ways: (1) judge their actual visual overlap directly from the displays — how much of each group's data lies among the other group's values; and (2) separately, find the difference between their centres and express it as a multiple of a clearly named measure of variability of either group, using matching measures (difference in means ÷ MAD, or difference in medians ÷ IQR), interpreting a larger multiple as centres that are further apart relative to the typical spread. Recognise that the same difference in centres means more when the variability is small, and that for similarly shaped, roughly symmetric, single-peaked distributions a larger multiple usually goes with less overlap — but that the ratio alone does not determine overlap: skew, clusters, gaps or outliers can make the visible overlap greater or smaller than the ratio suggests, so overlap is always checked on the display; and this simple ratio is only appropriate when the two variabilities are similar

topics.title: How samples vary
topics.description: Generate or compare several random samples of the same size from the same population (by drawing physically — returning and remixing the items before each new sample — from a list, or by simulation), observe that their estimates differ by chance, and use the spread of those estimates to judge how uncertain a single estimate or prediction is — distinguishing chance variation between random samples from the consistent error caused by a biased sampling method, and distinguishing variation between sample estimates from the variation among individual observations within a sample

topics.title: Scatter Graphs
topics.description: Plot bivariate data on a scatter graph with correctly labelled axes and appropriate scales; describe the correlation (positive, negative, none) and draw an estimated line of best fit where appropriate

topics.title: Scatter Graphs & Correlation
topics.description: Describe simple mathematical relationships between two variables using scatter graphs, identify positive, negative, or no correlation, and use a line of best fit to make predictions

topics.title: Finding halves and quarters
topics.description: Recognise, find, and name a quarter as one of four equal parts of an object, shape, or quantity, and use halves and quarters to share leftovers fairly with 2 or 4 sharers (e.g. 5 crackers between 2; 5 or 6 crackers among 4), seeing that two quarters of the same whole make a half

topics.title: Halves & Quarters of Shapes
topics.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares and describe them using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use 'two halves make one whole' to solve equal-group problems where each share is a half

topics.title: What Is a Half?
topics.description: Recognise, find, and name a half as one of two equal parts of an object, shape, or quantity

topics.title: Comparing fractions
topics.description: Compare and order unit fractions, and fractions with the same denominator; at an early stage, compare and order the shares when one whole is shared among different numbers of people, using drawings and words

topics.title: Decomposing a shape into more equal shares
topics.description: Understand that decomposing a shape into more equal shares creates smaller shares

topics.title: Fraction Notation
topics.description: Read, write, and use fraction notation correctly — fraction, numerator, denominator, unit fraction, non-unit fraction, proper fraction, improper fraction, mixed number, equivalent fraction, simplest form — and understand what each term describes, including the roles of the numerator and denominator in expressing parts of a whole

topics.title: Fractions of amounts
topics.description: Recognise, find, name, and write fractions 1/3, 1/4, 2/4, and 3/4 of a length, shape, set of objects, or quantity

topics.title: Halves, quarters and eighths
topics.description: Connect halves, quarters and eighths through repeated halving of shapes, objects, collections and events (such as half-time in a game or an activity split into equal time parts), and represent eighths

topics.title: Partitioning shapes into equal shares
topics.description: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares; describe shares as halves, thirds, and fourths; recognise that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Write simple fractions (e.g. 1/2 of 6 = 3) and recognise the equivalence of 2/4 and 1/2

topics.title: Comparing fractions
topics.description: Solve problems involving counting in tenths, fractions of quantities, equivalence, fraction addition/subtraction, and fraction comparison

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Recognise and show, using diagrams, equivalent fractions with small denominators

topics.title: Fractions of a whole
topics.description: Understand a fraction 1/b as the quantity formed by 1 part when a whole is partitioned into b equal parts; understand a/b as a parts of size 1/b

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Recognise and use fractions as numbers: place unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators on a number line

topics.title: Simple Fraction Sums
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator within one whole (e.g. 5/7 + 1/7 = 6/7)

topics.title: Tenths
topics.description: Count up and down in tenths; recognise that tenths arise from dividing an object into 10 equal parts and from dividing one-digit numbers or quantities by 10

topics.title: Unit fractions
topics.description: Recognise, find, and write fractions of a discrete set of objects: unit fractions and non-unit fractions with small denominators

topics.title: Adding Fractions (Same Denominator)
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions with the same denominator, including results greater than one whole (e.g. 5/8 + 6/8 = 11/8)

topics.title: Comparing fractions
topics.description: Compare two fractions with the same numerator or the same denominator by reasoning about size; record comparisons with >, =, or < symbols

topics.title: Decimal equivalents of tenths and hundredths
topics.description: Recognise and write decimal equivalents of any number of tenths or hundredths (e.g. 3/10 = 0.3, 27/100 = 0.27)

topics.title: Decimal & Percent Notation
topics.description: Read, write, and use decimal and percentage notation correctly — decimal, decimal point, tenths, hundredths, thousandths, percentage, per cent, % symbol, convert, terminating decimal — and understand the relationships between fractions, decimals, and percentages as three ways of expressing the same value

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Round decimals with one decimal place to the nearest whole number

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Compare numbers with the same number of decimal places up to two decimal places

topics.title: Decimals and fractions
topics.description: Solve simple measure and money problems involving fractions and decimals to two decimal places

topics.title: Dividing by 10 and 100
topics.description: Find the effect of dividing a one- or two-digit number by 10 and 100, identifying the value of the digits as ones, tenths, and hundredths

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Generate simple equivalent fractions and explain why they are equivalent using visual fraction models

topics.title: Equivalent fractions on a number line
topics.description: Understand two fractions as equivalent if they are the same size or the same point on a number line; recognise and show families of common equivalent fractions using diagrams

topics.title: Fraction-Decimal Equivalents
topics.description: Recognise and write decimal equivalents of 1/4, 1/2, and 3/4

topics.title: Fractions as parts of shapes
topics.description: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas and express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole

topics.title: Fractions as sums of unit fractions
topics.description: Understand a fraction a/b with a > 1 as a sum of fractions 1/b (e.g. 3/5 = 1/5 + 1/5 + 1/5)

topics.title: Fractions of amounts (harder)
topics.description: Solve problems involving increasingly harder fractions to calculate quantities, including non-unit fractions where the answer is a whole number

topics.title: Fractions of a whole
topics.description: Express whole numbers as fractions (e.g. 3 = 3/1) and recognise fractions equivalent to whole numbers (e.g. 4/4 = 1, 6/1 = 6)

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Represent fractions on a number line: partition the interval 0 to 1 into b equal parts to locate 1/b, then mark off a lengths of 1/b from 0 to locate a/b

topics.title: Tenths
topics.description: Count up and down in hundredths; recognise that hundredths arise when dividing an object by 100 or dividing tenths by 10

topics.title: Adding and subtracting mixed numbers
topics.description: Add and subtract mixed numbers with like denominators, including by converting to improper fractions or using properties of operations

topics.title: Adding fractions (different denominators)
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions with denominators that are multiples of the same number by finding a common denominator

topics.title: Addition and subtraction word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with like denominators, using visual models and equations

topics.title: Comparing Decimals
topics.description: Compare two decimals to hundredths (or up to three decimal places) by reasoning about size using place-value understanding; record with >, =, <

topics.title: Comparing fractions
topics.description: Compare and order fractions with different numerators and denominators by creating common denominators/numerators or comparing to a benchmark such as 1/2; justify conclusions with visual models

topics.title: Converting tenths to hundredths
topics.description: Express a fraction with denominator 10 as an equivalent fraction with denominator 100 and use this to add fractions with denominators 10 and 100 (e.g. 3/10 + 4/100 = 34/100)

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Round decimals with two decimal places to the nearest whole number and to one decimal place

topics.title: Decimals for Tenths & Hundredths
topics.description: Use decimal notation for fractions with denominators 10 or 100; read and write decimal numbers as fractions (e.g. 0.62 = 62/100, 0.71 = 71/100)

topics.title: Decimals to three places
topics.description: Solve problems involving numbers with up to three decimal places

topics.title: Equivalent fractions
topics.description: Explain why a fraction a/b is equivalent to (n×a)/(n×b) using visual models; use this principle to recognise and generate equivalent fractions, including tenths and hundredths

topics.title: Fraction Addition Concepts
topics.description: Understand addition and subtraction of fractions as joining and separating parts; decompose a fraction into a sum of fractions with the same denominator in more than one way

topics.title: Fractions of a whole
topics.description: Solve word problems involving multiplication of a fraction by a whole number using visual models and equations

topics.title: Mixed numbers and improper fractions
topics.description: Recognise mixed numbers and improper fractions; convert from one form to the other (e.g. 2/5 + 4/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5)

topics.title: Multiplying fractions
topics.description: Understand a/b as a multiple of 1/b; multiply proper fractions and mixed numbers by whole numbers, supported by visual models (e.g. 3 × 2/5 = 6/5 = 1 1/5)

topics.title: Percentage and decimal equivalents
topics.description: Solve problems requiring knowledge of percentage and decimal equivalents of 1/2, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5, 4/5 and fractions with denominators that are multiples of 10 or 25

topics.title: Tenths
topics.description: Recognise and use thousandths; relate them to tenths, hundredths, and their decimal equivalents (e.g. 1/1000 = 0.001, 35/1000 = 0.035)

topics.title: Understanding Percentages
topics.description: Understand the per cent symbol (%); know that per cent means ‘number of parts per hundred’; write percentages as a fraction with denominator 100 and as a decimal

topics.title: Adding Fractions (Unlike Denominators)
topics.description: Add and subtract fractions with unlike denominators (including mixed numbers) by replacing given fractions with equivalent fractions to produce a common denominator

topics.title: Area with Fractions
topics.description: Find the area of a rectangle with fractional side lengths by tiling with unit-fraction squares; show that the area equals the product of the side lengths

topics.title: Comparing fractions
topics.description: Compare and order fractions including fractions greater than 1, by converting to common denominators or using benchmarks

topics.title: Decimals and fractions
topics.description: Associate a fraction with division and calculate decimal fraction equivalents for simple fractions (e.g. 3/8 = 0.375); recall and use equivalences between simple fractions, decimals, and percentages in different contexts

topics.title: Dividing by Fractions
topics.description: Interpret and compute division of a whole number by a unit fraction (e.g. 4 ÷ 1/5 = 20); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain why the quotient is larger than the dividend

topics.title: Dividing fractions (unit fractions)
topics.description: Interpret and compute division of a unit fraction by a non-zero whole number (e.g. 1/3 ÷ 4 = 1/12); use visual models and the relationship between multiplication and division to explain the result

topics.title: Dividing unit fractions and whole numbers
topics.description: Solve real-world problems involving division of unit fractions by whole numbers and whole numbers by unit fractions, using visual models and equations

topics.title: Fractions of a whole
topics.description: Interpret a fraction as division of the numerator by the denominator (a/b = a ÷ b); solve word problems involving division of whole numbers leading to fractional or mixed-number answers

topics.title: Fraction Word Problems
topics.description: Solve word problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions with unlike denominators, using visual models and benchmark fractions to estimate and assess reasonableness

topics.title: Multiplication as scaling
topics.description: Interpret multiplication as scaling (resizing): compare the size of a product to a factor based on the size of the other factor without computing; explain the effect of multiplying by fractions greater than, equal to, or less than 1

topics.title: Multiplying fractions
topics.description: Multiply a fraction or whole number by a fraction, including proper fractions by proper fractions; interpret (a/b) × q as a parts of q partitioned into b equal parts; write answers in simplest form

topics.title: Real-world fraction multiplication
topics.description: Solve real-world problems involving multiplication of fractions and mixed numbers, using visual fraction models or equations

topics.title: Simplifying Fractions
topics.description: Use common factors to simplify fractions to their simplest form; use common multiples to express fractions with a common denominator

topics.title: Decimals and fractions
topics.description: Work interchangeably with terminating decimals and their corresponding fractions (such as 3.5 and 7/2 or 0.375 and 3/8); convert fluently between the two forms

topics.title: Dividing fractions
topics.description: Divide a fraction by a fraction using the 'keep-change-flip' method and visual models; interpret and solve word problems involving division of fractions by fractions

topics.title: Mixed & Improper Fractions

topics.title: Multiplying fractions
topics.description: Interpret fractions and percentages as operators — find a fraction or percentage of an amount by multiplying, understanding that 'of' means multiply (e.g., 3/4 of 200 = 3/4 × 200 = 150)

topics.title: 2-D shapes
topics.description: Recognise and name common 2-D shapes (circles, triangles, rectangles including squares)

topics.title: 3-D shapes
topics.description: Recognise and name common 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, pyramids, spheres, cylinders, cones)

topics.title: 3-D shapes
topics.description: Analyse and compare 2-D and 3-D shapes using informal language to describe sides, vertices, and other attributes

topics.title: Combining Simple Shapes
topics.description: Compose simple shapes to form larger shapes (e.g. two triangles make a rectangle)

topics.title: Positional Language
topics.description: Describe the position of objects using terms such as above, below, beside, in front of, behind, next to

topics.title: Building & Drawing Shapes
topics.description: Model shapes by building from components (e.g. sticks and clay balls) and by drawing

topics.title: Flat vs Solid Shapes
topics.description: Distinguish two-dimensional (flat) shapes from three-dimensional (solid) shapes

topics.title: Patterns & Sequences
topics.description: Order and arrange combinations of mathematical objects in patterns and sequences

topics.title: Turns & Directions
topics.description: Describe movement and direction, including whole, half, quarter, and three-quarter turns

topics.title: 2-D faces on 3-D shapes
topics.description: Identify 2-D shapes on the surface of 3-D shapes (e.g. a circle on a cylinder, a triangle on a pyramid)

topics.title: 2-D shapes
topics.description: Identify and describe properties of 2-D shapes including the number of sides and line symmetry in a vertical line

topics.title: Building with 3-D Shapes
topics.description: Compose three-dimensional shapes (cubes, right rectangular prisms, right circular cones, right circular cylinders) and create composite shapes; build new shapes from component shapes, including structures whose two halves match

topics.title: Composing Shapes
topics.description: Compose two-dimensional shapes (rectangles, squares, trapezoids, triangles, half-circles, quarter-circles) to create composite shapes, and compose new shapes from the composite shape

topics.title: Defining attributes of shapes
topics.description: Distinguish defining attributes of shapes (e.g. triangles are closed and three-sided) from non-defining attributes (e.g. colour, orientation, overall size)

topics.title: Edges, vertices, and faces
topics.description: Identify and describe properties of 3-D shapes including the number of edges, vertices, and faces

topics.title: Lines of symmetry
topics.description: Complete a simple symmetric figure with respect to a specific line of symmetry

topics.title: Position, direction, and movement
topics.description: Use mathematical vocabulary to describe position, direction, and movement, including straight lines and distinguishing rotation as a turn in terms of right angles (quarter, half, three-quarter turns, clockwise and anti-clockwise)

topics.title: Sorting 2-D and 3-D shapes
topics.description: Compare and sort common 2-D and 3-D shapes and everyday objects by their properties

topics.title: Understanding angles
topics.description: Recognise angles as a property of shape or a description of a turn

topics.title: 2-D shapes
topics.description: Draw 2-D shapes and make 3-D shapes using modelling materials; recognise 3-D shapes in different orientations and describe them

topics.title: 2-D shapes
topics.description: Identify lines of symmetry in 2-D shapes presented in different orientations; recognise line-symmetric figures and draw lines of symmetry

topics.title: Congruent shapes and objects by matching
topics.description: Identify congruent side lengths, angles and faces by matching them physically (tracing, overlaying, folding, comparing with a strip, fitting faces together) or mentally, within and between two-dimensional shapes and three-dimensional objects, and decide whether two shapes or two objects are congruent: the same size and the same shape, whatever their position or orientation (matching one face alone does not make two objects congruent)

topics.title: Parallel and perpendicular lines
topics.description: Identify horizontal and vertical lines and pairs of perpendicular and parallel lines

topics.title: Recognising and drawing shapes by attributes
topics.description: Recognise and draw shapes having specified attributes (e.g. a given number of angles or equal faces); identify triangles, quadrilaterals, pentagons, hexagons, and cubes

topics.title: Right Angles & Turns
topics.description: Identify right angles; recognise that two right angles make a half-turn, three make three-quarters, and four make a complete turn

topics.title: Classifying quadrilaterals
topics.description: Understand that shapes in different categories may share attributes defining a larger category; classify quadrilaterals (rhombuses, rectangles, squares) and draw examples of quadrilaterals not in those subcategories

topics.title: Coordinates
topics.description: Plot specified points on a coordinate grid and draw sides to complete a given polygon

topics.title: Describing Movements
topics.description: Describe movements between positions as translations of a given unit to the left/right and up/down

topics.title: First Quadrant Coordinates
topics.description: Describe positions on a 2-D grid as coordinates in the first quadrant

topics.title: Nets of 3-D Shapes

topics.description: Identify acute and obtuse angles; compare and order angles up to two right angles by size

topics.title: Why objects suit their uses
topics.description: Explain why the key features of 3-D objects (curved or flat faces, edges, vertices) make them suited to particular uses in everyday life

topics.title: 3-D shapes
topics.description: Identify 3-D shapes, including cubes and other cuboids, from 2-D representations

topics.title: Angle Sum Rules
topics.description: Know that angles at a point sum to 360° (one whole turn), angles on a straight line sum to 180°, and vertically opposite angles are equal; use these facts to find missing angles

topics.title: Approximating objects with shapes
topics.description: Represent and approximate composite shapes and objects in the environment using combinations of familiar 2-D shapes and 3-D objects

topics.title: Classifying shapes by line properties
topics.description: Classify two-dimensional figures based on the presence or absence of parallel or perpendicular lines, or angles of a specified size; recognise right triangles as a category

topics.description: Estimate and compare acute, obtuse, and reflex angles in degrees; classify angles by type and order them by size

topics.title: Lines, Rays & Angles

topics.description: Measure angles in whole-number degrees using a protractor; draw given angles and sketch angles of specified measure

topics.description: Recognise angle measure as additive; find unknown angles by adding or subtracting on a diagram using equations with a symbol for the unknown

topics.title: Regular and irregular polygons
topics.description: Distinguish between regular and irregular polygons based on reasoning about equal sides and equal angles

topics.title: Rotational symmetry
topics.description: Recognise rotational symmetry in shapes and designs, state how many times a shape matches itself in a full turn, and create patterns with line and rotational symmetry, including by rotating a motif in dynamic geometry software

topics.title: Straight, reflex and revolution angles
topics.description: Name, estimate and compare straight angles, reflex angles and revolutions alongside acute, right and obtuse angles, describing each by its relationship to a right angle (without measuring in degrees)

topics.title: Transformations on a Grid
topics.description: Identify, describe, and represent the position of a shape following a reflection or translation using appropriate language; know that the shape has not changed

topics.title: Understanding angles
topics.description: Use the properties of rectangles to deduce related facts and find missing lengths and angles

topics.title: What Is an Angle?
topics.description: Understand that an angle is a geometric shape formed by two rays sharing a common endpoint (vertex); recognise angles in real-life contexts and 2-D shapes

topics.title: 2-D shapes
topics.description: Draw 2-D shapes using given dimensions and angles, using a ruler and protractor accurately

topics.title: 3-D shapes
topics.description: Recognise, describe, and build simple 3-D shapes, including making nets

topics.title: Angles in triangles
topics.description: Find unknown angles in triangles, quadrilaterals, and regular polygons using angle sum properties

topics.title: Classifying shapes by properties
topics.description: Compare and classify geometric shapes based on their properties and sizes; understand that attributes belonging to a category also belong to all subcategories; classify two-dimensional figures in a hierarchy based on properties

topics.title: Coordinates
topics.description: Describe positions on the full coordinate grid (all four quadrants); use coordinates with negative values

topics.title: Parts of a circle
topics.description: Illustrate and name parts of circles, including radius, diameter, and circumference; know that the diameter is twice the radius

topics.title: Plotting points in the first quadrant
topics.description: Plot and read ordered pairs in the first quadrant of the coordinate plane; represent real-world and mathematical problems by graphing points and interpreting coordinate values in context

topics.title: The coordinate grid
topics.description: Understand a coordinate system defined by two perpendicular number lines (axes) with an origin at (0,0); know that an ordered pair (x, y) specifies a unique point where the first number gives horizontal distance and the second gives vertical distance from the origin

topics.title: Top, front and side views of objects

topics.title: Translating and reflecting shapes
topics.description: Draw and translate simple shapes on the coordinate plane; reflect shapes in the axes

topics.title: Understanding angles
topics.description: Recognise angles where they meet at a point, are on a straight line, or are vertically opposite; find missing angles using these properties

topics.title: 3-D shapes
topics.description: Use the properties of faces, surfaces, edges, and vertices of 3-D shapes (cubes, cuboids, prisms, cylinders, pyramids, cones, and spheres) to solve problems, including visualising cross-sections

topics.title: Geometry notation and sketching

topics.title: Properties of triangles and quadrilaterals
