topics.description: Calculate the circumference and area of circles using the formulae C = πd (or 2πr) and A = πr², and solve problems involving perimeters and areas of composite shapes that include circular parts

topics.title: Congruent triangles
topics.description: Know and use the criteria for triangle congruence (SSS, SAS, ASA, RHS), use standard labelling conventions for sides and angles of triangle ABC, and determine whether two triangles are congruent

topics.title: Ruler and compass constructions
topics.description: Use ruler and compasses to perform standard constructions: perpendicular bisector of a line segment, perpendicular to a line from or at a given point, and bisecting an angle

topics.title: Similarity and enlargement
topics.description: Understand similarity as a relationship where one shape is an enlargement of another; construct similar shapes by enlargement with a given scale factor and centre, with and without coordinate grids

topics.title: Surface area and volume of solids
topics.description: Solve real-world and mathematical problems involving the surface area and volume of right prisms (including triangular and trapezoidal prisms) and of solids composed of cubes and right prisms: find a prism's surface area as the two bases plus the rectangular side faces; find volume as base area × height, including bases that are composite polygons; for composite solids, add the volumes of the parts but find the surface area from the exposed faces only, subtracting the areas hidden where parts join; and decide whether a problem needs area, surface area or volume

topics.title: Which triangles are possible
topics.description: Decide whether given side and angle conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle, and explain why, predicting with a freehand sketch and testing by construction (ruler and protractor, compasses, or dynamic geometry software): three sides give exactly one triangle when each pair of sides adds to more than the third, and none otherwise — if the two shorter sides add to less than the longest, the construction arcs do not meet, and if they add to exactly the longest (e.g. 3, 4 and 7), the arcs touch only on the base line, so the sides lie flat in a straight line rather than forming a triangle; three angles must add to 180° and then fix only the shape, not the size, so many triangles fit (none if the sum is not 180°); two sides with the included angle, or two angles with the included side, give exactly one triangle; and two sides with an angle that is not between them can give two, one or no triangles

topics.title: Applying Pythagoras' theorem
topics.description: Apply Pythagoras’ Theorem (a² + b² = c²) to calculate unknown side lengths in right-angled triangles, including in real-world and coordinate-geometry contexts

topics.title: Trigonometry basics
topics.description: Use the trigonometric ratios sin, cos, and tan in right-angled triangles to find unknown sides and angles, including setting up the correct ratio for a given problem

topics.title: Early Maths Vocabulary
topics.description: Use mathematical words carefully when counting, comparing, and describing shapes and positions

topics.title: Showing Your Working
topics.description: Show and tell how a mathematical answer was found using objects, drawings, and spoken words

topics.title: Finding efficient methods
topics.description: Notice when a calculation or pattern repeats and use this to count more efficiently or predict results

topics.title: Hands-On Problem Solving
topics.description: Select and use familiar tools (concrete objects, fingers, ten frames) to help solve a mathematical problem

topics.title: Making Sense of Problems
topics.description: Make sense of a problem by identifying what is being asked, choosing concrete objects or pictures to represent the situation, and explaining a pathway to the solution

topics.title: Real-World to Maths Connections
topics.description: Move between a real-world situation and a mathematical representation using concrete objects, drawings, diagrams, tables, number sentences, or bar models

topics.title: Spotting mathematical patterns
topics.description: Notice simple patterns and structures: spot that changing order doesn't change the total, and recognise how numbers relate to each other

topics.title: Using objects to model real problems
topics.description: Use objects, drawings, or simple number sentences to represent a real-world situation (early mathematical modelling)

topics.title: Connecting maths to real life
topics.description: Represent real-world problems with number sentences, bar models, or diagrams, and interpret the mathematical result back in context; use the model to make a prediction, check it against the real situation and revise the model if it does not fit (early modelling cycle)

topics.title: Connecting Representations
topics.description: Move between real-world situations, drawings, and number sentences, explaining how each representation connects to the others (quantitative reasoning)

topics.title: Explaining Mathematical Reasoning
topics.description: With teacher prompting, explain and justify mathematical reasoning using drawings, number sentences, or words

topics.title: Generalising Patterns
topics.description: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: spot calculation patterns, describe rules for sequences, and predict results using known mathematical facts

topics.title: Guided Multi-Step Problem Solving
topics.description: With teacher guidance, make sense of multi-step and more complex problems by planning a pathway to the solution, identifying relevant information, and choosing appropriate operations

topics.title: Numbers on a number line
topics.description: Select and use appropriate tools and representations (number lines, hundred squares, rulers, part-whole models) to support problem-solving

topics.title: Precise Maths Communication
topics.description: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary, specify units, and use symbols accurately

topics.title: Shape patterns
topics.description: Look for and use mathematical structure: apply properties of operations, place-value patterns, and relationships between shapes to solve problems efficiently

topics.title: Working with money
topics.description: Model real-world problems involving measurement, money, and time by choosing appropriate representations and interpreting results in context

topics.title: Choosing the right strategy
topics.description: Select and use appropriate tools and representations strategically, including choosing between mental methods, jottings, formal algorithms, and calculators for arithmetic with multi-digit numbers, decimals, and fractions

topics.title: Extending Table Patterns
topics.description: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend multiplication table patterns, derive unknown facts from known ones, and describe rules for sequences

topics.title: Justifying mathematical reasoning
topics.description: Construct and follow multi-step mathematical arguments; identify errors in reasoning and explain why a method works or does not work

topics.title: Multi-Step Problem Solving
topics.description: With teacher support, make sense of multi-step problems involving larger numbers or mixed operations by breaking them into parts, choosing strategies, and checking answers for reasonableness — children at this stage are developing the habit with guidance; independent strategy evaluation comes later

topics.title: Shape patterns
topics.description: Look for and use mathematical structure: apply place-value patterns to three-digit operations, use multiplication/division relationships, and exploit shape properties to classify

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, and symbolic equations involving three-digit numbers and fractions, explaining what each part represents

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct place-value and fraction vocabulary, specify units in measurement answers, and use notation accurately

topics.title: Choosing mathematical tools
topics.description: Select and use appropriate tools and representations strategically: choose between mental, written, and diagrammatic methods; use calculators for checking; select fraction models suited to the task

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, number lines, and symbolic equations involving multiplication, fractions, and decimals, explaining what each representation shows

topics.title: Justifying mathematical reasoning
topics.description: Construct and present multi-step mathematical arguments; critique the reasoning of others and explain clearly why a method works or fails

topics.title: Mathematical Precision
topics.description: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct fraction/decimal vocabulary, name angle types accurately, specify units in measurement and money, and use notation (=, <, >, ÷, ×) correctly

topics.title: Modelling with multiplication and fractions
topics.description: Model real-world problems involving multiplication, area, fractions, and unit conversion by choosing appropriate representations and interpreting mathematical results in context

topics.title: Multi-Step Problem Solving
topics.description: Make sense of multi-step problems involving four operations, fractions, and area/volume by identifying sub-steps, choosing a strategy, and monitoring progress

topics.title: Times tables
topics.description: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend patterns in times tables and equivalent fractions, derive unknown facts from known facts efficiently, describe general rules

topics.title: Using a calculator well
topics.description: Use a calculator efficiently and appropriately to solve multi-step addition, subtraction, multiplication and division problems, deciding when a calculator is the best tool and checking the result with an estimate

topics.title: Using Mathematical Structure
topics.description: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit place-value patterns for ×10/×100, use the distributive property to break apart multiplications, apply fraction equivalence to compare and compute, use shape properties to classify quadrilaterals

topics.title: Choosing representations strategically
topics.description: Select and use tools and representations strategically: choose between mental methods, formal written methods, protractors, fraction strips, and diagrams based on the demands of the problem

topics.title: Complex Multi-Step Problems
topics.description: Make sense of complex multi-step problems involving large numbers, fractions, decimals, and percentages by analysing what is known and unknown, planning multi-step strategies, and evaluating reasonableness through estimation and inverse operations

topics.title: Fractions, Decimals & Percentages
topics.description: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit the relationship between fractions, decimals, and percentages; use factor pairs to simplify multiplication; apply angle facts to find unknowns; use properties of regular polygons systematically

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, number lines, bar models, and symbolic equations involving multi-digit multiplication, fractions, decimals, and percentages, explaining connections between representations

topics.title: Precise Maths Vocabulary
topics.description: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary for primes, factors, multiples, angle types, and polygon regularity; specify units including cm², m³, °; use notation for squares/cubes and percentages accurately

topics.title: Real-World Maths Modelling
topics.description: Model real-world problems involving scaling, unit conversion, area/perimeter, and percentage by selecting appropriate mathematical representations and interpreting results in context

topics.title: Reasoning with Equivalences
topics.description: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: extend patterns in equivalent fractions and percentage conversions, derive unknown facts from known facts, describe general rules for sequences and predict terms

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Construct and present logical mathematical arguments involving multiple steps; critique others' reasoning about fractions, angles, or calculations and clearly explain errors or alternative methods

topics.title: Advanced Maths Vocabulary
topics.description: Communicate with mathematical precision: use correct vocabulary for ratio, proportion, algebra, volume, coordinate geometry, and circle parts; specify units including cm³, m³, and miles/km; use notation for algebraic expressions and order of operations accurately

topics.title: Advanced Multi-Step Problems
topics.description: Make sense of complex multi-step problems involving ratio, proportion, algebra, negative numbers, and all four operations with fractions and decimals by analysing given and unknown quantities, planning solution strategies, and evaluating reasonableness using estimation and inverse operations

topics.title: Choosing Maths Tools
topics.description: Select and use tools and representations strategically: choose between mental methods, formal written methods, algebraic approaches, coordinate grids, and technology based on the demands of the problem

topics.title: Constructing mathematical arguments
topics.description: Construct and present logical mathematical arguments involving multiple steps and formal reasoning; critique others' reasoning about fractions, algebra, ratio, or geometry and clearly explain errors or alternative approaches

topics.title: Generalising with repeated reasoning
topics.description: Recognise and use repeated reasoning to generalise: describe algebraic rules for nth terms, use properties of operations to simplify, and verify generalisations with specific cases

topics.title: Order of operations
topics.description: Look for and use mathematical structure: exploit the hierarchy of 2-D shapes to deduce properties; use order of operations and algebraic structure to simplify expressions; connect fraction–decimal–percentage equivalences; use ratio structure to solve proportion problems efficiently

topics.title: Real-World Mathematical Modelling
topics.description: Model real-world problems involving ratio, scale, volume, unit conversion, and proportional reasoning with appropriate tools, diagrams, or equations

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Move fluently between real-world situations, diagrams, coordinate grids, algebraic expressions, tables, and symbolic equations involving fractions, ratio, and algebra, explaining connections between representations

topics.title: Comparing Capacity
topics.description: Compare and describe capacity and volume using language such as full, empty, more than, less than, half full

topics.title: Comparing durations
topics.description: Use comparative language for time: quicker, slower, earlier, later

topics.title: Comparing Lengths & Heights
topics.description: Compare two objects directly by length or height and describe the difference using language such as long, short, tall, longer, shorter, taller, double, half

topics.title: Measurable Attributes of Objects
topics.description: Describe and identify measurable attributes of objects such as length, height, weight, and capacity; use comparative language (longer, shorter, heavier, lighter, more, less)

topics.title: Measuring mass and weight
topics.description: Compare two objects directly by mass or weight and describe the difference using language such as heavy, light, heavier than, lighter than

topics.title: Ordering Events in Time
topics.description: Sequence events in chronological order using language such as before, after, next, first, today, yesterday, tomorrow, morning, afternoon, evening

topics.title: Capacity and volume
topics.description: Measure and begin to record capacity and volume using non-standard and standard units

topics.title: Coin Values
topics.description: Recognise and know the value of different coins and notes

topics.title: Days, Weeks, Months & Years
topics.description: Recognise and use language relating to dates, including days of the week, weeks, months, and years

topics.title: Hours, minutes and seconds
topics.description: Measure and begin to record time in hours, minutes, and seconds

topics.title: Measuring length and height
topics.description: Measure and begin to record lengths and heights using non-standard and standard units

topics.title: Measuring mass and weight
topics.description: Measure and begin to record mass/weight using non-standard and standard units

topics.title: Telling Time: Hours and Half Hours
topics.description: Tell and write the time to the hour and half past the hour on analogue clocks and digital displays (e.g. 3 o'clock = 3:00, half past 7 = 7:30), and draw clock hands to show these times, placing the hour hand halfway between two numbers for half past

topics.title: Adding money and giving change
topics.description: Find different combinations of coins that equal the same amount of money

topics.title: Area
topics.description: Measure areas by counting unit squares (square cm, square m, square in, square ft)

topics.title: Choosing measurement units
topics.description: Choose and use appropriate standard units to measure length (m/cm), mass (kg/g), temperature (°C), and capacity (litres/ml) to the nearest appropriate unit

topics.title: Comparing and ordering measurements
topics.description: Compare and order lengths, mass, and capacity and record results using >, <, and =

topics.title: Comparing mass and capacity indirectly
topics.description: Compare and order the mass and capacity of objects indirectly, using a balance or a third object or container as a go-between, and explain the reasoning

topics.title: Estimating capacity
topics.description: Estimate the capacity of containers by comparing them with a known measure and check by filling: informal units (e.g. cups or scoops) at an early stage, and litres and millilitres (e.g. against a 1-litre bottle, as in England Key Stage 2) when standard units are known; at the standard-unit stage, distinguish a container's capacity (how much it can hold) from the volume of liquid in it. Estimating the volume of solids with 1 cm³ cubes is covered in Counting Unit Cubes

topics.title: Estimating Lengths
topics.description: Estimate lengths by comparing with a known reference unit and check by measuring: informal units (e.g. paper clips, cubes, hand spans) at an early stage, and standard units (inches, feet, centimetres and metres, as in US Grade 2) when those units are known

topics.title: Measuring length
topics.description: Order three objects by length and compare the lengths of two objects indirectly using a third object

topics.title: Measuring length
topics.description: Measure the length of an object using same-size length units laid end to end with no gaps or overlaps

topics.title: Money Addition & Subtraction
topics.description: Solve simple money problems involving addition and subtraction, including giving change

topics.title: Money notation and units
topics.description: Recognise and use the symbols and notation for the main and smaller units of the local currency (for example £ and p, or $ and c), knowing that 100 of the smaller unit make 1 of the main unit, and combine amounts to make a particular value

topics.title: Number of minutes in an hour
topics.description: Know the number of minutes in an hour and the number of hours in a day

topics.title: Sequence intervals of time
topics.description: Compare and sequence intervals of time

topics.title: Telling time to 5 minutes
topics.description: Tell and write the time to five minutes on analogue clocks, including quarter past and quarter to the hour, write these times in digital form, and draw clock hands to show them

topics.title: Understanding Area
topics.description: Understand that a unit square has one square unit of area and that the area of a plane figure is the number of unit squares that cover it without gaps or overlaps

topics.title: Using a calendar
topics.description: Read a calendar to identify today's date and the day of the week for a given date, determine the number of days between two events, and use a supplied local calendar to find the holidays and season changes it marks

topics.title: Addition and subtraction word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems involving lengths within 100, using addition and subtraction with drawings and equations

topics.title: a.m. and p.m. times
topics.description: Tell and write times to five minutes on analogue and digital clocks with a.m. or p.m. (before or after midday), relating times to daily events and using the words morning, afternoon, evening, noon and midnight. Roman-numeral clock faces and the 24-hour clock are covered in Roman numeral and 24-hour clocks

topics.title: Calculating with measurements
topics.description: Measure, compare, add, and subtract lengths (m/cm/mm), mass (kg/g), and volume/capacity (l/ml) using standard units

topics.title: Comparing lengths by measuring
topics.description: Measure to determine how much longer one object is than another, expressing the length difference in terms of a standard length unit

topics.title: Comparing Time Durations
topics.description: Compare durations of events and calculate the time taken by particular events or tasks

topics.title: Giving Change
topics.description: Add and subtract amounts of money to give change, using both £ and p in practical contexts

topics.title: Measuring length
topics.description: Measure the length of an object by selecting and using appropriate tools such as rulers, yardsticks, metre sticks, and measuring tapes

topics.title: Measuring Perimeters
topics.description: Measure the perimeter of simple 2-D shapes

topics.title: Measuring & Plotting Lengths
topics.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest whole unit and display the data on a line plot

topics.title: Measuring with different units
topics.description: Measure the length of an object using two different length units and describe how the measurements relate to the size of the unit chosen

topics.title: Money word problems
topics.description: Solve word problems involving dollar bills, quarters, dimes, nickels, and pennies, using $ and ¢ symbols appropriately

topics.title: Quarter past and quarter to
topics.description: Recognise, read and show quarter past and quarter to the hour on an analog clock, linking each to a quarter turn of the minute hand

topics.title: Roman numeral and 24-hour clocks
topics.description: Tell and write the time from analogue clocks with Roman-numeral faces (I to XII, including IV, which some clocks show as IIII, and IX), knowing that the minute positions are the same as on a clock with ordinary numbers; and read and write times on 12-hour and 24-hour clocks, knowing that the 24-hour clock runs from 00:00 at midnight to 23:59. Times from 1:00 a.m. to 11:59 a.m. keep the same hour (7:05 a.m. = 07:05); times from 1:00 p.m. to 11:59 p.m. are 12 hours more (3:20 p.m. = 15:20). The 12 o'clock hour is the exception to both: 12:20 p.m., just after noon, stays 12:20, and 12:20 a.m., just after midnight, becomes 00:20. Fluent conversion between 12- and 24-hour times is developed in Year 4

topics.title: Smaller units for accuracy
topics.description: Choose a smaller uniform informal unit when a measurement needs to be more accurate, recognising that a smaller unit gives a larger count, for length, mass and capacity

topics.title: Time to the nearest minute
topics.description: Tell, write and estimate the time to the nearest minute on analogue and digital clocks, using vocabulary such as o'clock, a.m./p.m., morning, afternoon, noon and midnight; record and compare times and durations in seconds, minutes and hours

topics.title: Time Units and Calendar Facts
topics.description: Know the number of seconds in a minute and the number of days in each month, year, and leap year

topics.title: 12-hour and 24-hour time
topics.description: Read, write, and convert time between analogue and digital 12-hour and 24-hour clocks

topics.title: Area and the distributive property
topics.description: Use tiling to demonstrate the distributive property: the area of a rectangle with sides a and (b+c) equals a×b + a×c; use area models to represent the distributive property

topics.title: Area by Tiling
topics.description: Find the area of a rectangle by tiling it with unit squares and show that the result equals the product of the side lengths

topics.title: Area of compound shapes
topics.description: Recognise area as additive; find areas of rectilinear figures by decomposing into non-overlapping rectangles and summing their areas

topics.title: Area of rectangles by multiplication
topics.description: Multiply side lengths to find areas of rectangles and represent whole-number products as rectangular areas

topics.title: Converting measurement units
topics.description: Convert between different units of measure (e.g. kilometre to metre, hour to minute, minute to second, year to month, week to day)

topics.title: Elapsed time problems
topics.description: Solve word problems involving elapsed time by adding and subtracting time intervals in minutes, including using a number line

topics.title: Estimating and comparing money
topics.description: Estimate, compare, and calculate different measures including money in pounds and pence

topics.title: Halves and quarters
topics.description: Generate measurement data by measuring lengths to the nearest half and quarter inch; display the data on a line plot with a scale marked in whole numbers, halves, and quarters

topics.title: Measuring Liquids & Masses
topics.description: Measure and estimate liquid volumes and masses of objects using grams, kilograms, and litres; solve one-step word problems involving mass or volume

topics.title: Perimeters of polygons
topics.description: Solve problems involving perimeters of polygons: find perimeter from side lengths, find an unknown side length, and explore rectangles with same perimeter but different areas (or vice versa)

topics.title: Unit relationships and conversion tables
topics.description: Know relative sizes of measurement units within one system (km/m/cm/mm, kg/g, l/ml, hr/min/sec); convert between different metric units and express measurements in terms of a smaller unit; record equivalents in conversion tables

topics.title: Area and perimeter of rectangles
topics.description: Apply the area formula (l × w) and perimeter formula (2l + 2w) for rectangles including squares in real-world and mathematical problems; calculate and compare areas using standard units (cm², m²) and estimate areas of irregular shapes

topics.title: Comparing best buys
topics.description: Compare the value of products sold in different quantities or prices by working out and comparing unit prices (price per item or per unit of mass or volume), using a calculator where appropriate, and explain which is the better buy

topics.title: Counting Unit Cubes
topics.description: Measure and estimate the volume of solids by counting unit cubes: build cuboids from 1 cm³ cubes and count them, count the cubes in models and drawings (including hidden cubes), estimate how many cubes will fill a box and check by filling it, and record volumes in cubic units (cm³, in³, ft³ or improvised units)

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Solve word problems involving distances, time intervals, liquid volumes, masses, and money using the four operations with fractions or decimals; represent with diagrams including number lines

topics.title: Measurement Line Plots
topics.description: Make a line plot to display measurement data in fractions of a unit (1/2, 1/4, 1/8); solve problems involving addition and subtraction of fractions using line plot data

topics.title: Metric & Imperial Conversion
topics.description: Understand and use approximate equivalences between metric units and common imperial units (inches, pounds, pints)

topics.title: Perimeter of Compound Shapes
topics.description: Measure and calculate the perimeter of composite rectilinear shapes in centimetres and metres

topics.title: Reading between scale marks
topics.description: Interpret unmarked and partial units on scaled instruments and read digital instruments when measuring length, mass, capacity, duration and temperature, using appropriate units

topics.title: Telling time to the minute
topics.description: Solve problems involving converting between units of time (hours↔minutes, minutes↔seconds, years↔months, weeks↔days)

topics.title: What volume means
topics.description: Recognise volume as an attribute of solid figures; understand that a unit cube (side length 1 unit) has 'one cubic unit' of volume and can be used to measure volume; a solid packed with n unit cubes has volume n cubic units

topics.title: Area of Triangles & Parallelograms
topics.description: Find the area of parallelograms and triangles by relating them to rectangles: rearrange a parallelogram (cut off a triangle and move it) into a rectangle with the same base and perpendicular height; see a right triangle as half of a rectangle and any triangle as half of a parallelogram (or as two right triangles); use the resulting formulae A = b × h for parallelograms and A = ½ × b × h for triangles, always using the perpendicular height rather than a slanted side, including when the height falls outside an obtuse triangle; and recognise when an area formula can be used (rectangles, parallelograms, triangles) and when another method is needed, such as counting or estimating squares for an irregular shape

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Convert among different-sized standard measurement units within a given system (e.g. 5 cm to 0.05 m) using decimal notation to up to three decimal places; convert between smaller and larger units of length, mass, volume, and time

topics.title: Measurement Conversions
topics.description: Solve problems involving the calculation and conversion of units of measure, using decimal notation and multi-step reasoning in real-world contexts

topics.title: Miles & Kilometres
topics.description: Convert between miles and kilometres using the approximate relationship (5 miles ≈ 8 km)

topics.title: Perimeter
topics.description: Recognise that shapes with the same area can have different perimeters and vice versa; explore this relationship systematically

topics.title: Volume as additive
topics.description: Recognise volume as additive; find volumes of composite solid figures made of two or more non-overlapping right rectangular prisms

topics.title: Volume of cuboids
topics.description: Find the volume of right rectangular prisms by packing with unit cubes and show it equals l × w × h (or base area × height); apply V = l × w × h and V = B × h to solve real-world problems; calculate, estimate, and compare volumes of cubes and cuboids in standard units (cm³, m³); and recognise that the formula applies to cuboids, while an irregular solid built from cubes must be counted or split into cuboids

topics.title: Area by splitting shapes
topics.description: Find the area of polygons such as trapezoids, kites, rhombuses, irregular quadrilaterals and other rectilinear or non-rectilinear polygons by decomposition or composition: decompose the shape into rectangles and triangles and add the parts, or compose it into an enclosing rectangle and subtract the pieces outside; record the dimensions used for each piece, check that the pieces neither overlap nor leave gaps, and apply this to real-world problems such as floor plans, gardens and signs, giving answers in square units. The focus is the decomposition and composition strategy, which works for any polygon whether or not a dedicated formula is known

topics.title: Discounts and GST
topics.description: Solve and estimate financial problems in Australian dollars involving percentage discounts and adding the 10% GST to prices given before GST (recognising that GST-inclusive prices already contain it), using a calculator or spreadsheet where appropriate

topics.title: Surface area using nets
topics.description: Represent right rectangular prisms, triangular prisms and pyramids with rectangular or triangular bases using nets made of rectangles and triangles; use the solid's dimensions to label every face on the net; find the surface area as the sum of the face areas, in square units; distinguish surface area (the area covering the outside) from volume (the space inside); and apply this to real-world problems such as wrapping, painting or making boxes, including deciding which faces to include (e.g. an open-topped box)

topics.title: Volume with fraction lengths
topics.description: Find the volume of a right rectangular prism with fractional edge lengths by packing it with cubes whose edge is a suitable unit fraction of a unit (e.g. 1/2 or 1/4), working out the volume of one such cube (a cube with 1/2-unit edges has volume 1/8 cubic unit), counting the cubes and multiplying; show that this gives the same result as multiplying the edge lengths; and apply V = l × w × h and V = B × h with fractional or mixed-number edge lengths in real-world and mathematical problems

topics.title: Division as equal sharing
topics.description: Understand division as sharing equally into groups or as grouping (how many groups of a given size can be made)

topics.title: Arrays for multiplication
topics.description: Use arrays to represent multiplication and division situations

topics.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
topics.description: Understand multiplication as repeated addition and grouping equal sets

topics.title: Commutative Multiplication
topics.description: Understand and apply the commutative property of multiplication and recognise that division is not commutative

topics.title: Multiplication as repeated addition
topics.description: Solve problems involving multiplication and division using arrays, repeated addition, mental methods, and known facts

topics.title: Odd and even numbers
topics.description: Recognise odd and even numbers

topics.title: Reading ×, ÷, and = Symbols
topics.description: Read, write, and interpret the symbols ×, ÷, and = in multiplication and division number sentences

topics.title: Times tables
topics.description: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 2, 5, and 10 multiplication tables

topics.title: Arrays for multiplication
topics.description: Use addition to find the total number of objects arranged in rectangular arrays with up to 5 rows and 5 columns; write an equation to express the total as a sum of equal addends

topics.title: Multi-Step Multiply & Divide
topics.description: Solve problems involving multiplication and division, including scaling problems and correspondence problems where n objects are connected to m objects

topics.title: Rows & Columns in Rectangles
topics.description: Partition a rectangle into rows and columns of same-size squares and count to find the total number of them

topics.title: Times tables
topics.description: Recall and use multiplication and division facts for the 3, 4, and 8 multiplication tables

topics.title: Written Multiplication & Division
topics.description: Write and calculate mathematical statements for multiplication and division using known tables, including two-digit × one-digit, using mental and progressing to formal written methods

topics.title: All times tables to 12×12
topics.description: Recall multiplication and division facts for multiplication tables up to 12 × 12

topics.title: Division as Unknown Factor
topics.description: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem (e.g. find 32 ÷ 8 by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8)

topics.title: Factor Pairs & Commutativity
topics.description: Recognise and use factor pairs and commutativity in mental calculations

topics.title: Fluent multiplication and division facts
topics.description: Fluently multiply and divide within 100 using strategies such as the relationship between multiplication and division

topics.title: Mental multiplication and division
topics.description: Use place value, known and derived facts to multiply and divide mentally, including multiplying by 0 and 1, dividing by 1, and multiplying together three numbers

topics.title: Multiplication and Division Word Problems
topics.description: Use multiplication and division within 100 to solve word problems involving equal groups, arrays, and measurement quantities

topics.title: Multiplicative Comparison
topics.description: Interpret a multiplication equation as a comparison (e.g. 35 = 5 × 7 means 35 is 5 times as many as 7); represent verbal statements of multiplicative comparisons as equations

topics.title: Multiply & Add Problems
topics.description: Solve problems involving multiplying and adding, including using the distributive law, integer scaling problems, and harder correspondence problems

topics.title: Multiplying by Tens
topics.description: Multiply one-digit whole numbers by multiples of 10 in the range 10–90 using strategies based on place value and properties of operations

topics.title: Patterns in Times Tables
topics.description: Identify arithmetic patterns (including patterns in the addition table or multiplication table) and explain them using properties of operations

topics.title: Properties of Operations
topics.description: Apply properties of operations (commutative, associative, distributive) as strategies to multiply and divide

topics.title: Unknown in Multiplication & Division
topics.description: Determine the unknown whole number in a multiplication or division equation relating three whole numbers (e.g. 8 × ? = 48, ? × 6 = 42)

topics.title: What Division Means
topics.description: Interpret whole-number quotients (e.g. 56 ÷ 8 as the number of objects in each share or the number of equal groups)

topics.title: What Multiplication Means
topics.description: Interpret products of whole numbers (e.g. 5 × 7 as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7)

topics.title: Written Multiplication
topics.description: Multiply two-digit and three-digit numbers by a one-digit number using formal written layout

topics.title: Division with remainders
topics.description: Solve multi-step word problems using the four operations with whole numbers, including interpreting remainders in context; represent with equations using a letter for the unknown; check with estimation

topics.title: Factors, multiples, and primes
topics.description: Find all factor pairs for a whole number in the range 1–100; identify common factors and common multiples of two numbers; use these concepts to solve problems

topics.title: Factors, multiples, and primes
topics.description: Solve problems involving multiplication and division using knowledge of factors, multiples, squares, and cubes

topics.title: Long multiplication
topics.description: Multiply a whole number of up to four digits by a one-digit number, and multiply two two-digit numbers, using formal written methods including long multiplication; illustrate with area models

topics.title: Mental multiplication and division
topics.description: Multiply and divide numbers mentally drawing upon known facts, including related facts and place-value adjustments

topics.title: Multiplicative Comparison
topics.description: Solve word problems involving multiplicative comparison using drawings and equations with a symbol for the unknown number

topics.title: Multiplying and dividing
topics.description: Multiply and divide whole numbers and those involving decimals by 10, 100, and 1000

topics.title: Odd and even number rules
topics.description: Explain and use the properties of odd and even numbers when adding, subtracting and multiplying, e.g. odd + odd = even, odd + even = odd, and any whole number multiplied by an even number is even

topics.title: Prime numbers
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of prime numbers, prime factors, and composite numbers; establish whether a number up to 100 is prime; recall prime numbers up to 19

topics.title: Shape patterns
topics.description: Generate a number or shape pattern that follows a given rule; identify apparent features of the pattern not explicit in the rule and explain informally why they occur

topics.title: Short division with remainders
topics.description: Divide numbers up to four digits by a one-digit number using short division (and place-value/array strategies); interpret remainders appropriately for the context

topics.title: Square and cube numbers
topics.description: Recognise and use square numbers and cube numbers, and the notation for squared (²) and cubed (³)

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Solve problems involving scaling by simple fractions and problems involving simple rates

topics.title: Brackets in Expressions
topics.description: Use parentheses, brackets, or braces in numerical expressions and evaluate expressions containing these grouping symbols

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Multiply one-digit numbers with up to two decimal places by whole numbers (e.g. 3.47 × 6)

topics.title: Dividing by two-digit numbers
topics.description: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit number using formal written short division where appropriate, interpreting remainders according to context

topics.title: Division with Decimals
topics.description: Use written division methods in cases where the answer has up to two decimal places; divide decimals to hundredths by whole numbers

topics.title: Division with remainders
topics.description: Divide numbers up to 4 digits by a two-digit divisor using formal written long division, interpreting remainders as whole numbers, fractions, or by rounding as appropriate

topics.title: Estimation to check answers to calculations
topics.description: Use estimation to check answers to calculations and determine, in the context of a problem, an appropriate degree of accuracy

topics.title: Factor algorithms and spreadsheets
topics.description: Create and use algorithms with steps and decisions, and digital tools such as spreadsheets, to experiment with factors, multiples and divisibility, and describe the patterns that emerge

topics.title: Long multiplication
topics.description: Fluently multiply multi-digit whole numbers (up to 4 digits by 2 digits) using the formal written method of long multiplication

topics.title: Mental calculation strategies
topics.description: Perform mental calculations including with mixed operations and large numbers, using strategies such as partitioning, compensation, and derived facts

topics.title: Multiplying and dividing
topics.description: Multiply and divide numbers by 10, 100, and 1000 giving answers up to three decimal places, understanding that digits shift position in the place-value chart

topics.title: Multi-step problems: choosing operations
topics.description: Solve problems involving addition, subtraction, multiplication, and division, deciding which operations and methods to use and why; solve multi-step problems in contexts

topics.title: Order of operations
topics.description: Understand and apply the conventional order of operations (PEMDAS/BODMAS) to carry out calculations involving the four operations

topics.title: Rounding Answers
topics.description: Solve problems which require answers to be rounded to specified degrees of accuracy

topics.title: Writing Number Sentences
topics.description: Write simple numerical expressions that record calculations with numbers, and interpret numerical expressions without evaluating them (e.g. recognise that 3 × (18932 + 921) is three times as large as 18932 + 921)

topics.title: Estimating to check decimals
topics.description: Use estimation and rounding to check the reasonableness of answers when multiplying and dividing decimals (including by multiples of powers of 10), identifying misplaced decimal points

topics.title: Factors, multiples, and primes
topics.description: Use the concepts and vocabulary of prime numbers, factors, multiples, common factors, common multiples, highest common factor (HCF), lowest common multiple (LCM), and prime factorisation including product notation and the unique factorisation property

topics.title: Priority of operations
topics.description: Use conventional notation for the priority of operations including brackets, powers, roots, and reciprocals; apply BIDMAS/BODMAS consistently to evaluate complex numerical expressions

topics.title: Sign Rules for Multiplication
topics.description: Multiply and divide with positive and negative integers and rational numbers, understanding the rules for the sign of the product or quotient

topics.title: Using inverse operations
topics.description: Recognise and use relationships between operations including inverse operations; use these relationships to check answers and simplify calculations

topics.title: Number Words to Twenty
topics.description: Read and write number words from one to twenty

topics.title: Ordering numbers to 20
topics.description: Name, represent and order numbers from 0 to at least 20 using physical and virtual materials (number cards, on-screen ten frames and number tracks) and numerals

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers to 100
topics.description: Read and write numerals from 0 to 100, and describe the different ways numbers are used in everyday life (to count, measure, put things in order or label them)

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers to 20
topics.description: Read and write numerals from 0 to 20

topics.title: The teen numbers
topics.description: Understand that the teen numbers (11–19) are composed of ten ones and some further ones (early place value)

topics.title: 10 More or 10 Less
topics.description: Mentally find 10 more or 10 less than a given two-digit number without counting

topics.title: A Hundred Is Ten Tens
topics.description: Understand that 100 can be thought of as a bundle of ten tens — called a 'hundred'

topics.title: A Ten Is Ten Ones
topics.description: Understand that 10 can be thought of as a bundle of ten ones — called a 'ten'

topics.title: Comparing and ordering numbers
topics.description: Compare and order two-digit numbers, and numbers across 100 up to 120, using the symbols >, =, and <, based on place value understanding

topics.title: Number Words to 100
topics.description: Read and write numbers to at least 100 in words

topics.title: Place value understanding and number facts
topics.description: Use place value understanding and number facts to solve problems

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers to 120
topics.description: Count to 120 starting at any number less than 120; read and write numerals to 120

topics.title: Renaming two-digit numbers
topics.description: Partition and rename two-digit numbers in standard and non-standard ways (e.g. 34 = 3 tens 4 ones = 2 tens 14 ones) using physical and virtual base-ten materials, recognising that the total stays the same

topics.title: Representing numbers to 120
topics.description: Identify, represent and estimate numbers to 120 using different representations: place a number on a number line marked in tens, represent it with base-ten blocks or bundles of ten (tens and ones, including numbers just past 100 such as 112 as a hundred, a ten and two ones), drawings, bead strings or number charts, with physical or virtual materials, and estimate 'about how many' objects in a set before counting to check

topics.title: The multiples of 10
topics.description: Understand that the multiples of 10 (10, 20, 30 … 90) represent one to nine tens and 0 ones

topics.title: The two digits of a two-digit number
topics.description: Understand that the two digits of a two-digit number represent amounts of tens and ones

topics.title: 10 or 100 More or Less
topics.description: Find 10 or 100 more or less than a given number up to 1000

topics.title: Odd or Even
topics.description: Determine whether a group of objects (up to 20) has an odd or even number of members

topics.title: Ordering Numbers to 1000
topics.description: Compare and order numbers up to 1000 using >, =, and < symbols, based on place-value understanding

topics.title: Place Value to 1000
topics.description: Solve number problems and practical problems involving place value of numbers up to 1000

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers to 1000
topics.description: Read and write numbers to 1000 in numerals, number names, and expanded form

topics.title: Representing numbers to 1000
topics.description: Identify, represent and estimate three-digit numbers using different representations: place a number on a 0–1000 number line marked only in hundreds or unmarked, estimate the value of a marked point, and represent a number with base-ten blocks (hundreds, tens and ones), a place-value chart and a drawing, including numbers with a zero digit and non-standard partitions

topics.title: The multiples of 100
topics.description: Understand that the multiples of 100 (100–900) each represent a number of hundreds with 0 tens and 0 ones

topics.title: The three digits of a three-digit number
topics.description: Understand that the three digits of a three-digit number represent amounts of hundreds, tens, and ones

topics.title: 1000 More or Less
topics.description: Find 1000 more or less than a given number

topics.title: Comparing Large Numbers
topics.description: Order and compare numbers beyond 1000

topics.title: Negative Numbers
topics.description: Count backwards through zero to include negative numbers

topics.title: Numbers to 10,000
topics.description: Identify, represent, and estimate numbers up to 10,000 using different representations

topics.title: Place value of each digit
topics.description: Recognise the place value of each digit in a four-digit number (thousands, hundreds, tens, and ones)

topics.title: Place Value Problem-Solving
topics.description: Solve number and practical problems involving place value with increasingly large positive numbers

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers
topics.description: Read, write, order, and compare whole numbers up to at least 1,000,000 using base-ten numerals, number names, expanded form, and place-value understanding

topics.title: Roman numerals to 100
topics.description: Read Roman numerals to 100 (I to C) and understand that the numeral system changed over time to include zero and place value

topics.title: Rounding to 10, 100, 1000
topics.description: Round any number to the nearest 10, 100, or 1000

topics.title: Counting forwards and backwards
topics.description: Count forwards and backwards in steps of powers of 10 (10, 100, 1000, 10,000, 100,000) for any given number up to 1,000,000

topics.title: Negative numbers in context
topics.description: Interpret negative numbers in context (temperature, sea level, bank balance); count forwards and backwards with positive and negative whole numbers, including through zero

topics.title: Place Value × 10 Pattern
topics.description: Recognise that in a multi-digit whole number, a digit in one place represents ten times what it represents in the place to its right (e.g. 700 ÷ 70 = 10)

topics.title: Roman numerals to 1000
topics.description: Read Roman numerals to 1000 (M) and recognise years written in Roman numerals

topics.title: Rounding Large Numbers
topics.description: Round any whole number up to 1,000,000 to the nearest 10, 100, 1,000, 10,000, or 100,000 using place-value understanding

topics.title: Working with Large Numbers
topics.description: Solve number and practical problems involving reading, writing, ordering, comparing, and rounding whole numbers up to 1,000,000

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Round decimals to any place using place-value understanding; round any whole number to a required degree of accuracy

topics.title: Measuring temperature
topics.description: Use negative numbers in context (temperature, finance, sea level); calculate intervals across zero

topics.title: Numbers to Ten Million
topics.description: Solve number and practical problems involving reading, writing, ordering, comparing, rounding, and negative numbers up to 10,000,000

topics.title: Patterns with Powers of Ten
topics.description: Explain patterns in zeros when multiplying by powers of 10 and in decimal-point placement when multiplying/dividing by a power of 10; use whole-number exponents to denote powers of 10 (e.g. 10³ = 1000)

topics.title: Place Value × 10 and ÷ 10
topics.description: Recognise that in a multi-digit number, a digit in one place represents 10 times as much as in the place to its right and 1/10 of what it represents in the place to its left

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers
topics.description: Read, write, and compare decimals to thousandths using base-ten numerals, number names, and expanded form; compare using >, =, < based on place-value meaning

topics.title: Reading and writing numbers to 10,000,000
topics.description: Read, write, order, and compare numbers up to 10,000,000 and determine the value of each digit

topics.title: Reading Decimal Places
topics.description: Identify the value of each digit in numbers given to three decimal places (e.g. in 4.378, the 7 represents 7 hundredths)

topics.title: Absolute value as distance
topics.description: Understand the absolute value of a rational number as its distance from zero on the number line; interpret absolute value as magnitude in real-world contexts; distinguish absolute value comparisons from ordering statements

topics.title: Decimal place value
topics.description: Round numbers and measures to an appropriate degree of accuracy including to a specified number of decimal places or significant figures

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Understand and use place value for decimals, measures, and integers of any size; extend the number system to include all positive and negative integers, decimals, and fractions on a single number line

topics.title: Fractions on a number line
topics.description: Order positive and negative integers, decimals, and fractions on a number line; use the symbols =, ≠, <, >, ≤, ≥ to compare values including negative numbers and mixed representations

topics.title: Square and cube numbers
topics.description: Use integer powers and associated real roots (square, cube, and higher); recognise powers of 2, 3, 4, and 5; distinguish between exact representations of roots and their decimal approximations

topics.title: Estimating by rounding
topics.description: Use approximation through rounding to estimate answers and calculate possible resulting errors expressed using inequality notation a < x ≤ b; understand upper and lower bounds of rounded values

topics.title: Powers of Ten Notation
topics.description: Interpret and compare numbers in standard form A × 10ⁿ where 1 ≤ A < 10 and n is an integer; convert between ordinary numbers and standard form

topics.title: Number Sets & Infinity
topics.description: Appreciate the infinite nature of the sets of integers, real numbers, and rational numbers; position integers on a number line and distinguish between rational and irrational numbers

topics.title: Likelihood Language
topics.description: Use probability language to describe and compare the likelihood of everyday events using words such as certain, likely, even chance, unlikely, impossible

topics.title: Simple Chance Experiments
topics.description: Conduct simple probability experiments — flipping a coin, rolling a die, pulling coloured counters from a bag — record results, and compare experimental outcomes with expected theoretical outcomes

topics.title: Equally Likely Outcomes
topics.description: Understand that 'equally likely' means every outcome has exactly the same chance of occurring; identify whether a given situation has equally likely outcomes (a fair coin, a fair die, a spinner with equal sections) or unequally likely outcomes (a bag with more of one colour, a spinner with unequal sections)

topics.title: Ordering Likelihoods
topics.description: Compare the likelihood of different events and order them from least to most likely — including situations with unequal outcomes such as a bag with more of one colour than another, or a spinner with sections of different sizes — and explain reasoning using informal language

topics.title: Experimental vs Theoretical
topics.description: Run repeated probability experiments and compare experimental (relative frequency) results with theoretical predictions; understand and demonstrate that as the number of trials increases, the experimental probability tends towards the theoretical probability — and that short runs can give very different results

topics.title: Independent and dependent events
topics.description: Identify whether events in chance experiments and everyday situations are independent (one does not affect the other) or dependent (the first outcome changes the chances of the next)

topics.title: Probability as a Fraction
topics.description: Describe the probability of simple equally-likely outcomes using unit fractions: the probability of rolling a 6 on a fair die is 1/6, flipping heads is 1/2, picking one specific colour from three equally represented colours is 1/3; place these fractional probabilities on a 0-to-1 probability scale

topics.title: Calculating Simple Probability
topics.description: Calculate the probability of a simple event with equally likely outcomes using the formula: probability = number of favourable outcomes ÷ total number of possible outcomes; express the result as a fraction in its simplest form; apply to rolling dice, drawing from bags, and other simple chance situations

topics.title: Experimental probability
topics.description: Record, describe, and analyse the frequency of outcomes from probability experiments to develop an understanding of relative frequency as an estimate of probability

topics.title: Probabilities Sum to One
topics.description: Understand that when all possible outcomes of a trial are listed, their probabilities must add up to 1; use this to find the probability of an event NOT happening: P(not A) = 1 − P(A); apply this shortcut to avoid counting all unfavourable outcomes directly

topics.title: The 0-to-1 Probability Scale
topics.description: Understand probability as a measure expressed as a number between 0 (impossible) and 1 (certain); place events on the probability scale; express probabilities as fractions, decimals, and percentages

topics.title: Complementary events
topics.description: Understand and apply the rule that probabilities of all mutually exclusive outcomes sum to one; use this to find the probability of a complementary event (P(not A) = 1 − P(A))

topics.title: The Probability Scale
topics.description: Understand probability as a measure on a scale from 0 (impossible) to 1 (certain); use the language of probability including likely, unlikely, certain, and impossible

topics.title: Probability models
topics.description: Develop a probability model (a list of all the outcomes of a chance process with a probability for each, adding to 1) and use it to find probabilities of events: a uniform model gives every outcome the same probability (e.g. selecting a student at random from a class); a non-uniform model uses probabilities estimated from the observed frequencies of a chance process (e.g. how a tossed paper cup lands); compare a model's probabilities with observed frequencies and, when they disagree, explain whether the difference is plausibly chance variation or a sign that the model does not fit (e.g. a biased die or unequal spinner sections)

topics.title: Sets & Venn Diagrams
topics.description: Enumerate sets and their unions and intersections systematically using tables, grids, and Venn diagrams to organise and count outcomes

topics.title: Simulating chance events
topics.description: Design and use a simulation to estimate the probability of a compound event: choose a random device (coins, dice, spinners, counters drawn with replacement, random-digit tables, or calculator or software random numbers) and a mapping whose probabilities match the situation; define one complete trial (what is generated and when the trial stops) and the event being counted; run many trials; and estimate the probability as the event's relative frequency. Explain why the model fits (each simulated outcome has the same probability as the real one, and successive outcomes are independent when the real ones are), and why different runs give different estimates that become more consistent as the number of trials grows; where a theoretical value can be found (e.g. with a tree diagram), compare it with the estimate

topics.title: Tree diagrams
topics.description: Generate theoretical sample spaces for single and combined events using listing, tables, and tree diagrams, and calculate theoretical probabilities as the number of favourable outcomes divided by the total number of equally likely outcomes

topics.title: Venn Diagrams and Counting Outcomes
topics.description: Construct and interpret Venn diagrams with two or three sets to organise and count outcomes; use systematic listing and the product rule for counting to enumerate all possible outcomes of combined events

topics.title: Bar Models for Ratios
topics.description: Represent ratio and proportion problems using bar models (rectangular strips divided into equal parts labelled with quantities) and tape diagrams (segmented strips showing part-to-part and part-to-whole relationships); use these visual models to set up and solve unequal sharing, scaling, and percentage problems — drawing the diagram first, then reading off the answer

topics.title: Percentages
topics.description: Know and use the vocabulary of ratio and proportion — ratio, proportion, percentage, scale, equivalent, unequal, relative size, part-to-part, part-to-whole, and out of — and understand the difference between ratio (comparing parts to parts) and proportion (comparing a part to the whole)

topics.title: Calculating Percentages
topics.description: Solve problems involving the calculation of percentages of amounts (e.g. 15% of 360) and the use of percentages for comparison

topics.title: Ratio Problems
topics.description: Solve problems involving the relative sizes of two quantities where missing values can be found by using integer multiplication and division facts

topics.title: Scale and similar shapes
topics.description: Solve problems involving similar shapes where the scale factor is known or can be found

topics.title: Understanding fractions
topics.description: Solve problems involving unequal sharing and grouping using knowledge of fractions and multiples

topics.title: Compound Units
topics.description: Use compound units such as speed (distance ÷ time), unit pricing (cost ÷ quantity), and density (mass ÷ volume); solve problems involving compound units

topics.title: Dividing Quantities by Ratio
topics.description: Divide a given quantity into two parts in a given part:part or part:whole ratio, and express the division as a fraction of the whole

topics.title: One Quantity as a Fraction
topics.description: Express one quantity as a fraction of another where the result may be less than 1 or greater than 1, and interpret the meaning in context

topics.title: Percentages as Fractions
topics.description: Define percentage as 'number of parts per hundred'; interpret percentages and percentage changes as a fraction or a decimal; express one quantity as a percentage of another; compare quantities using percentages; work with percentages greater than 100%

topics.title: Proportional Reasoning Vocabulary
topics.description: Know and use advanced vocabulary of multiplicative reasoning — direct proportion, inverse proportion, ratio, rate, unit rate, compound unit, scale factor — accurately in problem-solving contexts

topics.title: Proportion Graphs
topics.description: Represent proportional relationships using double number lines (two parallel number lines aligned at 0) and ratio tables; recognise that equivalent ratios generate straight lines through the origin when graphed

topics.title: Ratio Notation
topics.description: Use ratio notation to describe the relationship between two or more quantities, simplify ratios to their simplest form, and convert between ratio and fraction representations

topics.title: Scale drawings and maps
topics.description: Use a scale, given as a ratio (e.g. 1:50), as a statement such as '1 cm represents 2 m', or as a scale factor, to work out actual lengths from a scale drawing or map and drawing lengths from actual lengths; reproduce a scale drawing at a different scale by finding each new drawing length, either through the actual length or from the ratio of the two scales; and solve map, room-plan and design problems with consistent units, converting between mm, cm, m and km before or after scaling. Areas from scale drawings and the area factor are developed in the follow-on topic Area from scale drawings

topics.title: Unit Conversions
topics.description: Convert freely between related standard units of measurement (time, length, area, volume/capacity, mass) using decimal notation to up to three decimal places where appropriate

topics.title: Area from scale drawings
topics.description: Find actual areas from a scale drawing or map, either by converting each drawing length to an actual length before multiplying or by using the area factor; explain why, when every length is multiplied by a scale factor k, areas are multiplied by k² (both dimensions are scaled), and avoid the mistake of applying the length factor to an area; convert between square units consistently (e.g. 1 m² = 10,000 cm²); and apply this to map, room-plan and design problems such as flooring, turf, paint or land area

topics.title: Percentages
topics.description: Solve problems involving percentage increase, percentage decrease, finding the original value after a percentage change, and calculating simple interest

topics.title: Proportion
topics.description: Recognise and solve problems involving direct proportion (as one quantity increases, the other increases at a constant rate) and inverse proportion (as one increases, the other decreases), including graphical and algebraic representations

topics.title: Ratio Notation and Relationships
topics.description: Understand that a multiplicative relationship between two quantities can be expressed as a ratio; use ratio notation; simplify ratios
